title: Reduction to constructible prime torsion
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $C$ be a scheme proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] of dimension at most one, and let $F$ be a torsion abelian sheaf on $C_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf], so that $(C,F)$ is a curve coefficient pair [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting] with $C$ proper. Let $i:C_{\mathrm{red}}\to C$ be the reduction of $C$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction], and fix an algebraically closed extension $k'/k$. For a curve coefficient pair $(D,G)$ over $k$ write $\rho^q_{k'/k}(D,G):H^q(D_{\Et},G)\to H^q((D_{k'})_{\Et},G_{k'})$ for the pullback map [def-weil-pbc-extension-pullback] along the projection $D_{k'}=D\times_kk'\to D$, i.e. the pullback map of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] for that morphism.

Assume: for every prime number $r$ and every constructible sheaf $G$ of $\mathbf F_r$-modules on $(C_{\mathrm{red}})_{\Et}$ (constructible in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] with $\Lambda=\mathbf F_r$; such a $G$ is killed by $r$, hence torsion, and $(C_{\mathrm{red}},G)$ is a curve coefficient pair with $C_{\mathrm{red}}$ reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and proper), the map $\rho^q_{k'/k}(C_{\mathrm{red}},G)$ is bijective for every $q\ge0$.

Then $\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,F)$ is bijective for every $q\ge0$. In particular, if the hypothesis holds for every algebraically closed extension $k'/k$, then assertion $\mathcal C_7(C,F)$ [def-weil-pbc-C7] (the seventh of the eight curve assertions) holds.

The coefficient passage runs through filtered colimits of constructible sheaves, the primary decomposition of a constructible sheaf killed by an integer, and the exact sequences $0\to G[r]\to G\to G/G[r]\to0$.

proof.text: (Reduction to $C_{\mathrm{red}}$.) Write $C_0=C_{\mathrm{red}}$ and $F_0=i^{-1}F$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism], $C_0$ is reduced and $i$ is a surjective closed immersion and a universal homeomorphism. $C_0$ is proper over $k$ (a closed immersion followed by a proper morphism [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]) and has the same underlying space as $C$, so $\dim C_0\le1$. $F_0$ is torsion: $i^{-1}$ is exact [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact], so $i^{-1}(F[n])=\ker(n:F_0\to F_0)=F_0[n]$, and $i^{-1}$ preserves colimits [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-preserves-colimits], so $i^{-1}(c_F)$ is the map $c_{F_0}:\varinjlim_nF_0[n]\to F_0$ of [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf], an isomorphism since $c_F$ is. Hence $(C_0,F_0)$ is a curve coefficient pair with $C_0$ proper and reduced.

proof.text:
(The comparison square.) Let $\pi:C_{k'}\to C$ and $\pi_0:(C_0)_{k'}\to C_0$ be the projections and $i'=i\times_kk':(C_0)_{k'}\to C_{k'}$, so that $i\circ\pi_0=\pi\circ i'$. The morphism $i'$ is a universal homeomorphism: for a morphism $Y'\to C_{k'}$, $(C_0)_{k'}\times_{C_{k'}}Y'\cong C_0\times_CY'$ over $Y'$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and the projection of the latter to $Y'$ is a homeomorphism because $i$ is a universal homeomorphism [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism]. By [prop-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-topos] (Stacks 03SI) the pullback maps $i^*:H^q(C,F)\to H^q(C_0,F_0)$ and $i'^*:H^q(C_{k'},\pi^{-1}F)\to H^q((C_0)_{k'},i'^{-1}\pi^{-1}F)$ are bijective. By the composition rule of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] (item 4), with the isomorphisms $c:\pi_0^{-1}i^{-1}\cong(i\pi_0)^{-1}$ and $c':i'^{-1}\pi^{-1}\cong(\pi i')^{-1}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition], both composites equal $(i\pi_0)^*=(\pi i')^*$:
$$H^q(c_F)\circ\rho^q_{k'/k}(C_0,F_0)\circ i^*=H^q(c'_F)\circ i'^*\circ\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,F).$$
Here $H^q(c_F)$ and $H^q(c'_F)$ are bijective, being $H^q$ of isomorphisms of sheaves (functoriality of $H^q$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]). Hence $\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,F)$ is bijective as soon as $\rho^q_{k'/k}(C_0,F_0)$ is. From now on replace $(C,F)$ by $(C_0,F_0)$: $C$ is reduced, and it remains to show that $\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,F)$ is bijective for every torsion $F$ on $C$ and every $q$.

source.place: Theorem 03SC (theorem-vanishing-affine-curves), proof, first sentence, with Proposition 03SI (proposition-topological-invariance); the square is written out by the agent

proof.text:
(Two out of three.) Let $u:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes and $0\to G_1\to G\to G_2\to0$ a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves on $X_{\Et}$. If $u^*:H^q(X,G_j)\to H^q(Y,u^{-1}G_j)$ is bijective for $j=1,2$ and every $q\ge0$, then $u^*:H^q(X,G)\to H^q(Y,u^{-1}G)$ is bijective for every $q\ge0$. Indeed, by [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-cohomology-long-exact-ladder] the maps $u^*$ form a commutative diagram between the exact rows
$$H^{q-1}(X,G_2)\xrightarrow{\delta}H^q(X,G_1)\to H^q(X,G)\to H^q(X,G_2)\xrightarrow{\delta}H^{q+1}(X,G_1)$$
and the corresponding row on $Y$ (for $q=0$ the first group is replaced by $0$ on both rows), whose four outer vertical maps are bijective; the five lemma in abelian groups [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] gives the middle one. Applied to the split sequences $0\to G_1\to G_1\oplus G_2\to G_2\to0$ and by induction on the number of summands, the same holds for finite direct sums. This is the part of Stacks Lemma 0A5C (lemma-ses-statements) concerning statement (7), proved there by the long exact sequence.

source.place: Lemma 0A5C (lemma-ses-statements), proof ('immediate from the definitions and the long exact sequence of cohomology'), for statement (7)

proof.text: (Filtered colimits.) Let $(G_a)_{a\in A}$ be a filtered system of torsion abelian sheaves on $C_{\Et}$ with colimit $G$ in $\Ab(C_{\Et})$. If $\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,G_a)$ is bijective for every $a$ and $q$, so is $\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,G)$. Indeed $\pi^{-1}$ preserves colimits [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-preserves-colimits], so $\pi^{-1}G=\varinjlim_a\pi^{-1}G_a$ with coprojections $\pi^{-1}$ of those of $G$, and the $\pi^{-1}G_a$ are torsion (as in step 1). $C$ and $C_{k'}$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated curves (of finite type over a field), so by [lemma-weil-pbc-curve-filtered-cohomology] the maps $\kappa:\varinjlim_aH^q(C,G_a)\to H^q(C,G)$ and $\kappa':\varinjlim_aH^q(C_{k'},\pi^{-1}G_a)\to H^q(C_{k'},\pi^{-1}G)$ induced by $H^q$ of the coprojections are bijective. Naturality of $\pi^*$ in the sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] (item 3), applied to the coprojections $G_a\to G$, gives $\rho^q(C,G)\circ\kappa=\kappa'\circ\varinjlim_a\rho^q(C,G_a)$; a filtered colimit of bijections is bijective, so $\rho^q(C,G)$ is bijective.

source.place: Theorem 03SC (theorem-vanishing-affine-curves), proof, first paragraph: 'Taking cohomology commutes with colimits, see Lemma 03Q5. Moreover, pullback via X_{k'} -> X commutes with colimits as a left adjoint'

proof.text: (Reduction to constructible sheaves killed by an integer.) $F$ is torsion, so $F=\varinjlim_nF[n]$ over the positive integers ordered by divisibility, a filtered colimit [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf]; each $F[n]$ is killed by $n$, hence torsion. By step 4 it suffices to treat an abelian sheaf $H$ with $nH=0$. Such an $H$ is a sheaf of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules, $\mathbf Z/n$ a finite ring, on the scheme $C$ of finite type over $k$, so by [lem-kun-03sa] (Stacks 03SA(3)) $H=\varinjlim_bH_b$ is a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Sheaves of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules are the abelian sheaves killed by $n$, a full subcategory of $\Ab(C_{\Et})$ closed under colimits (multiplication by $n$ on a colimit is the colimit of the zero maps), so this is also a filtered colimit in $\Ab(C_{\Et})$, of torsion sheaves. By step 4 again it suffices to show that $\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,G)$ is bijective for every $n\ge1$ and every constructible sheaf $G$ of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules. (Stacks applies 03SA(2), whose proof is exactly this passage $F=\bigcup F[n]$ followed by 03SA(3); taking the two colimits one after the other avoids assembling one index category.)

source.place: Theorem 03SC (theorem-vanishing-affine-curves), proof, first paragraph, with Lemma 03SA (lemma-torsion-colimit-constructible), parts (2) and (3) and the proof of (2)

proof.text: (Primary decomposition.) Let $G$ be a constructible sheaf of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules and $n=\prod_{\ell\mid n}\ell^{e_\ell}$. By the Chinese remainder theorem there are $\epsilon_\ell\in\mathbf Z/n$ with $\epsilon_\ell\equiv1\bmod\ell^{e_\ell}$ and $\epsilon_\ell\equiv0\bmod\ell'^{e_{\ell'}}$ for $\ell'\ne\ell$; they are orthogonal idempotents with sum $1$, so $G=\bigoplus_\ell\epsilon_\ell G$ and $\epsilon_\ell G=G[\ell^{e_\ell}]=\ker(\ell^{e_\ell}:G\to G)$. Each $G[\ell^{e_\ell}]$, the kernel of an endomorphism of a constructible $\mathbf Z/n$-module sheaf, is constructible by [thm-constructible-serre] ($\Lambda=\mathbf Z/n$). A sheaf of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules killed by a divisor $m$ of $n$ is a sheaf of $\mathbf Z/m$-modules, and it is constructible as a $\mathbf Z/m$-module sheaf iff it is as a $\mathbf Z/n$-module sheaf: the strata are the same, and on a stratum a local isomorphism with a constant sheaf $\underline M$ of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules is one of $\mathbf Z/m$-modules, $M$ being killed by $m$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], [def-constructible-finite-locally-constant]. By step 3 (finite direct sums, with $u=\pi$) it suffices to treat a constructible sheaf of $\mathbf Z/\ell^e$-modules, $\ell$ prime, $e\ge1$.

source.place: Theorem 03SC (theorem-vanishing-affine-curves), proof, second paragraph: 'Writing F = F_1 + ... + F_r where F_i is l_i-primary ... we may assume that l^n kills F'

proof.text: (Induction on the exponent.) Let $G$ be a constructible sheaf of $\mathbf Z/\ell^e$-modules; we show by induction on $e\ge1$ that $\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,G)$ is bijective for all $q$. For $e=1$, $G$ is a constructible sheaf of $\mathbf F_\ell$-modules on the reduced proper curve $C=C_{\mathrm{red}}$ and this is the hypothesis. For $e\ge2$ consider $0\to G[\ell]\to G\to G/G[\ell]\to0$, exact in $\Ab(C_{\Et})$ (kernels and cokernels of sheaves of $\mathbf Z/\ell^e$-modules are computed in abelian sheaves). $G[\ell]=\ker(\ell:G\to G)$ and $G/G[\ell]=\operatorname{coker}(G[\ell]\to G)$ are constructible sheaves of $\mathbf Z/\ell^e$-modules by [thm-constructible-serre] ($\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^e$). $G[\ell]$ is killed by $\ell$, and $G/G[\ell]$ is killed by $\ell^{e-1}$, since for a local section $s$ one has $\ell\cdot\ell^{e-1}s=\ell^es=0$, i.e. $\ell^{e-1}s\in G[\ell]$. By the change of rings in step 6 they are constructible sheaves of $\mathbf F_\ell$-modules, resp. of $\mathbf Z/\ell^{e-1}$-modules, so $\rho^q$ is bijective for both (hypothesis, resp. induction), and step 3 with $u=\pi$ gives it for $G$.

source.place: Theorem 03SC (theorem-vanishing-affine-curves), proof, second paragraph: 'consider the exact sequence 0 -> F[l] -> F -> F/F[l] -> 0. Thus we see that it suffices to assume that F is l-torsion'

proof.text: (Conclusion.) Steps 6 and 7 give the bijectivity of $\rho^q_{k'/k}(C_{\mathrm{red}},G)$ for every constructible sheaf of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules $G$; steps 4 and 5 extend it to every torsion sheaf on $C_{\mathrm{red}}$, in particular to $i^{-1}F$; step 2 transfers it to $\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,F)$, for every $q\ge0$. If this holds for every algebraically closed $k'/k$, it is assertion $\mathcal C_7(C,F)$ by the definition [def-weil-pbc-C7].

split_report.summary: Statement made precise against Stacks 03SC: a fixed algebraically closed k'/k, the pullback rho^q_{k'/k} of def-weil-pbc-extension-pullback / def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback, hypothesis on all constructible F_r-module sheaves on C_red for all primes r, conclusion rho^q(C,F) bijective for all q, hence C_7(C,F) [def-weil-pbc-C7] when it holds for all k'. stmt_deps: grab-bag def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves replaced by def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf (torsion) and def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf (constructible, Lambda = F_r); def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions replaced by its component def-weil-pbc-C7; added def-weil-pbc-curve-setting, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-pbc-extension-pullback, def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback and the new Mathlib leaf def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction (X.nilradical.subscheme). The imported one-paragraph proof is replaced by eight steps following the first two paragraphs of the proof of 03SC: (1)-(2) reduction to C_red via the new lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism (Stacks 054M) and prop-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-topos (03SI, same unit, Lean closed) instead of thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance (other unit), with the comparison square written out through the composition rule of lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial; (3) two-out-of-three for pullback isomorphisms through the new lem-weil-pbc-pullback-cohomology-long-exact-ladder (pullback maps commute with the connecting maps; no node existed) and lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma: this replaces lemma-weil-pbc-eight-curve-devissage, whose statement concerns the conjunction of all eight assertions and cannot be applied to C_7 alone; (4) filtered colimits through lemma-weil-pbc-curve-filtered-cohomology (used only for its first sentence; the compatibility with the ground-field extension is derived from naturality and lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-preserves-colimits); (5) F = colim F[n] and lem-kun-03sa (03SA(3), Lambda = Z/n) taken one after the other; (6) primary decomposition with thm-constructible-serre; (7) induction on the exponent with 0 -> G[l] -> G -> G/G[l] -> 0; (8) conclusion. The unreachable lemma-weil-pbc-curve-constructible-primary-reduction states the same reduction (for separated curves, extension invariance in general) with an uncited proof: it duplicates this node and is not cited; lemma-weil-pbc-curve-dense-open-reduction is the next reduction of 03SC (constructible F_l-sheaves to j_!G) and belongs to the parent's split, not to this statement.
